Reproducible research with UCDP data

Source: vignettes/reproducible-research.Rmd
reproducible-research.Rmd

A reproducible UCDP workflow records the exact release, inspects the imported structure, checks analytical assumptions, and retains the corresponding documentation. ucdpR keeps these tasks separate so that each decision remains visible.

library(ucdpR)

conflicts <- data.frame(
  conflict_id = c(1, 2, 3),
  year = c(2020, 2021, 2021),
  location = c("A", "B", "C"),
  low = c(0, 2, 1),
  best = c(1, 3, 2),
  high = c(2, 4, 3),
  latitude = c(10, 20, 30),
  longitude = c(40, 50, 60)
)

Describe the object and its coverage

ucdp_metadata() gives a compact record of dimensions and available temporal or coordinate coverage. Imported UCDP objects additionally report their source record, checksum, retrieval time, and package version.

ucdp_metadata(conflicts, dataset = "Synthetic conflict data")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 20
#>   dataset             version variant format file_name source_url catalog_source
#>   <chr>               <chr>   <chr>   <chr>  <chr>     <chr>      <chr>         
#> 1 Synthetic conflict… NA      NA      NA     NA        NA         NA            
#> # ℹ 13 more variables: retrieved_at <chr>, md5 <chr>, ucdpR_version <chr>,
#> #   n_rows <int>, n_columns <int>, year_min <int>, year_max <int>,
#> #   date_min <chr>, date_max <chr>, latitude_min <dbl>, latitude_max <dbl>,
#> #   longitude_min <dbl>, longitude_max <dbl>

ucdp_schema() works at the variable level and is useful before joins, transformations, or model preparation.

schema <- ucdp_schema(conflicts)
schema[c("variable", "class", "n_missing", "n_unique", "minimum", "maximum")]
#> # A tibble: 8 × 6
#>   variable    class     n_missing n_unique minimum maximum
#>   <chr>       <chr>         <int>    <int> <chr>   <chr>  
#> 1 conflict_id numeric           0        3 1       3      
#> 2 year        numeric           0        2 2020    2021   
#> 3 location    character         0        3 NA      NA     
#> 4 low         numeric           0        3 0       2      
#> 5 best        numeric           0        3 1       3      
#> 6 high        numeric           0        3 2       4      
#> 7 latitude    numeric           0        3 10      30     
#> 8 longitude   numeric           0        3 40      60

Validate assumptions without altering data

Validation checks are applied only when their required variables are present. The result separates a compact summary from record-level issues.

validation <- ucdp_validate(conflicts, key = "conflict_id")
validation$valid
#> [1] TRUE
validation$summary
#> # A tibble: 5 × 3
#>   check       status  n_issues
#>   <chr>       <chr>      <int>
#> 1 keys        pass           0
#> 2 dates       skipped        0
#> 3 fatalities  pass           0
#> 4 coordinates pass           0
#> 5 codes       skipped        0
validation$issues
#> # A tibble: 0 × 6
#> # ℹ 6 variables: check <chr>, severity <chr>, row <int>, column <chr>,
#> #   value <chr>, message <chr>

Warnings identify observations for inspection; they do not establish that UCDP made a coding error. With strict = TRUE, warnings also make the overall validation result invalid, which can be useful in automated pipelines.

Aggregate events and retain fatality uncertainty

Fatality estimates should be aggregated as a low, best, and high triplet rather than reducing every observation to its best estimate alone.

ucdp_fatalities(conflicts, by = "year")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>    year n_observations n_complete n_missing fatalities_low fatalities_best
#>   <dbl>          <int>      <int>     <int>          <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1  2020              1          1         0              0               1
#> 2  2021              2          2         0              3               5
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: fatalities_high <dbl>

conflict_year <- ucdp_aggregate(
  conflicts,
  unit = "conflict-year"
)
conflict_year
#> # A tibble: 3 × 8
#>   conflict_id  year n_events n_fatality_complete n_fatality_missing
#>         <dbl> <int>    <int>               <int>              <int>
#> 1           1  2020        1                   1                  0
#> 2           2  2021        1                   1                  0
#> 3           3  2021        1                   1                  0
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: fatalities_low <dbl>, fatalities_best <dbl>,
#> #   fatalities_high <dbl>

ucdp_aggregate() also supports country, PRIO-GRID, and dyad units with yearly or monthly periods. Common entity and fatality columns are detected, while id, date, low, best, and high provide explicit overrides.

Construct complete panels transparently 

panel_events <- data.frame(
  conflict_id = c(1, 1, 2),
  year = c(2020, 2022, 2021),
  low = c(0, 1, 2), best = c(1, 2, 3), high = c(2, 3, 4)
)

panel <- ucdp_panel(
  panel_events,
  unit = "conflict-year",
  start = 2020,
  end = 2022,
  fill = "zero"
)
panel[c("conflict_id", "year", "n_events", ".ucdp_observed", ".ucdp_fill")]
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>   conflict_id  year n_events .ucdp_observed .ucdp_fill 
#>         <dbl> <int>    <int> <lgl>          <chr>      
#> 1           1  2020        1 TRUE           observed   
#> 2           1  2021        0 FALSE          zero_filled
#> 3           1  2022        1 TRUE           observed   
#> 4           2  2020        0 FALSE          zero_filled
#> 5           2  2021        1 TRUE           observed   
#> 6           2  2022        0 FALSE          zero_filled

Rows introduced to complete the panel remain identifiable. A zero-filled row does not prove that UCDP observed a true zero; it records the analyst’s chosen completion rule. Use fill = "missing" when unobserved combinations should remain missing, and supply universe when the panel must include entities that never appear in the event data.

Retain provenance with live data 

prio <- ucdp_get("prio", version = "25.1", format = "csv")
ucdp_metadata(prio)
ucdp_schema(prio)
ucdp_validate(prio)

If the original source file should remain alongside the analysis, use ucdp_download() and store it in a project directory rather than relying on a temporary import.

Keep documentation with the release

Codebooks explain variables and coding rules; version histories explain changes between releases; citation guidance records the attribution requested by UCDP.

ucdp_codebook(
  "prio", version = "25.1", dest_dir = "documentation"
)
ucdp_version_history(
  "prio", version = "25.1", dest_dir = "documentation"
)
ucdp_cite("prio")

Exact historical documentation is returned only when UCDP explicitly lists a matching artifact. The package does not silently substitute a current codebook for an older release.

Use publication-specific replication files

UCDP’s replication archive is distinct from its ordinary dataset catalog. It contains frozen files associated with particular publications.

replication <- ucdp_replication_catalog(
  query = "Georeferenced", year = 2025, type = "data"
)

paths <- ucdp_replication_download(
  "ged", version = "25.1", year = 2025,
  dest_dir = "replication"
)

attr(paths, "ucdp_records")
attr(paths, "md5")

A practical project record

For each empirical analysis, retain at least:

  1. the dataset name, exact version, and variant;
  2. the original file or its source URL and checksum;
  3. the retrieval date and ucdpR version;
  4. the matching codebook and version history;
  5. validation output and explicit filtering decisions; and
  6. UCDP’s requested citation.

These records do not eliminate all sources of uncertainty, but they make the analytical input reconstructable and revisions auditable.
